description: Physics-lumped transient: cavity-receiver thermal ODE (absorbed - convection - radiation^4 - conduction) coupled to a Carnot-limited Stirling engine (Beale/internal-loss model) giving net electrical power.

unit.name: 25 kWe Stirling Dish Unit (SES SunCatcher / EuroDish class)
unit.source: Stine & Diver (1994), SAND93-7026 'A Compendium of Solar Dish/Stirling Technology'; Mancini et al. (2003), J. Sol. Energy Eng. 125(2), 135-151; Nepveu et al. (2009), Sol. Energy 83(1), 81-89.

A_dish.note: Dish reflective aperture area (~11 m rim diameter), EuroDish/SunCatcher class

eta_optical.note: Peak optical efficiency = reflectance * intercept * shading * cleanliness (Stine & Diver 1994)

A_rec.note: Cavity receiver aperture/wall area exposed to losses

eps_rec.note: Receiver cavity effective emissivity for re-radiation

h_cav.note: Natural/forced convection coefficient at receiver cavity (Nepveu 2009)

U_cond.note: Conduction loss coefficient through receiver insulation

T_sky_offset.note: Sky temperature = T_amb - offset for radiative sink

m_rec.note: Lumped thermal mass of receiver tube/cavity assembly

cp_rec.note: Effective specific heat of receiver metal (Inconel/SS, ~460-540 J/kgK)

dT_receiver.note: Temperature drop from receiver wall to Stirling working-gas hot end

T_approach.note: Stirling cold-end (cooler) approach above ambient via radiator

eta_internal.note: Stirling 2nd-law / regenerator+mechanical effectiveness vs ideal Carnot (relative Carnot efficiency, Stine & Diver 1994)

P_parasitic_kw.note: Cooling fan + tracking + controls parasitic draw while running

Q_engine_min_kw.note: Minimum net thermal input to receiver gas for engine to run (de-stroke threshold)

T_engine_on_c.note: Heater-head startup temperature: engine de-stroked (Q_engine=0) below this so the receiver can warm up; real dish-Stirling units only engage once the head is hot (Stine & Diver 1994)

P_rated_kw.note: Rated net electrical output per dish
